reference: Documented contract oracle: the published implementation documentation documents the non-interactive stdin/result behavior, result channels, checklist output modes, mixedform field types, gauge input, and zero-second pause. Its whiptail_doc supplies the help text; Bash's builtin metadata table declares the short_doc as whiptail, and Bash help formats that short_doc followed by the indented long doc. Expected bytes and statuses below are taken from those source contracts plus Bash type/help builtin behavior, not from candidate output. No GNU/POSIX-standardized whiptail command is used as a fake oracle, and no PTY rendering parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata for whiptail.
Non-interactive yes/no status mapping for Y and a non-yes response.
Inputbox result routing to default stderr and an explicit output file descriptor.
Menu tag output and --notags item-text output.
Mixedform editable, password-type, and readonly fields in pipe mode.
Gauge input lines and the documented immediate zero-second pause.
exclusions: There are no parity cases: the Bash builtin metadata and documented pipe-mode extension have no matching GNU/POSIX-standardized CLI oracle; the external whiptail UI is not treated as an equivalent oracle.
PTY key handling, terminal drawing, resizing, and scrolling are deferred because the provided fixture runner starts fixtures without a controlling terminal.
The untested pipe-mode widget families include radiolist, treeview, inputmenu, form, textbox, and tailbox; the tested subset is not a complete whiptail compatibility claim.

cases.purpose: Confirm whiptail is registered as a Bash builtin, as required by the loadable contract.
Confirm Bash help exposes the documented whiptail alias note.
cases.stdout:
whiptail: whiptail
    whiptail-compatible alias for dialog. See `help dialog`.

cases.purpose: Check the documented non-interactive rule that Y selects Yes with status 0 and a non-yes response selects No with status 1.
cases.script:
if printf 'Y
' | whiptail --yesno 'Continue?' 8 30; then yes_rc=0; else yes_rc=$?; fi
if printf 'n
' | whiptail --yesno 'Continue?' 8 30; then no_rc=0; else no_rc=$?; fi
printf '%s/%s
' "$yes_rc" "$no_rc"

cases.purpose: Check that inputbox emits its entered line to the default result channel and that --output-fd selects another open descriptor.
cases.script:
printf 'default value\n' | whiptail --inputbox Value 8 30 2>default.txt
printf 'fd value\n' | whiptail --output-fd 3 --inputbox Value 8 30 3>fd.txt
printf 'default value\n' > expected-default
printf 'fd value\n' > expected-fd
cmp default.txt expected-default
cmp fd.txt expected-fd
printf 'default value|fd value\n'

cases.purpose: Check menu selection returns the chosen tag by default and the item's text under --notags.
cases.script:
printf 'second\n' | whiptail --stdout --menu 'Pick one' 10 40 2 first 'First item' second 'Second item' >tag.txt
IFS= read -r tag <tag.txt
printf 'second\n' | whiptail --stdout --notags --menu 'Pick one' 10 40 2 first 'First item' second 'Second item' >item.txt
IFS= read -r item <item.txt
printf '%s|%s\n' "$tag" "$item"
printf 'second\n' > expected-tag
printf 'Second item\n' > expected-item
cmp tag.txt expected-tag
cmp item.txt expected-item

cases.purpose: Check selected checklist tags are emitted one per line when --separate-output is requested.
cases.script: printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' | whiptail --stdout --separate-output --checklist 'Pick items' 12 40 4 alpha 'Alpha item' off beta 'Beta item' off gamma 'Gamma item' off

cases.purpose: Check pipe mode reads one line for each editable mixedform field, skips input for a readonly field, and emits final values in field order.
Check the documented gauge pipe input accepts both percent-suffixed and bare integer lines and produces no result text.
Check the documented non-interactive zero-second pause returns immediately without output.
Exercise terminal keyboard behavior and result/cancel handling for yesno, inputbox, and passwordbox.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed PTY mock with a controlling terminal, fixed TERM and dimensions, and scripted key bytes to cover Tab/Enter/Esc, cursor editing, and password masking. The current fixture runner has no PTY input or terminal transcript facility.

cases.purpose: Exercise terminal navigation, toggling, defaults, and selection output for menu, checklist, radiolist, treeview, and inputmenu.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed PTY mock with fixed TERM/terminfo and scripted arrow/space/Enter/Esc input, plus a pinned external whiptail release for the terminal transcript oracle. No PTY is provided by this fixture runner.

cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed PTY mock with fixed terminal dimensions, a bounded keyboard stream, and a pinned external whiptail transcript oracle; file-backed textbox/tailbox fixtures must remain relative and private. The current runner cannot provide a controlling terminal.
